Stata reference · R reference

correlate

Pearson correlations (complete cases)

Stata 

correlate x1 x2 x3

R tidystata 

corr(data, x1, x2, x3)

Differs from Stata Uses one common complete-case sample within each group, like Stata correlate. Returns r and n without p-values; .wide = TRUE gives a lower-triangular table. Optional .wt supports frequency or analytic weights; zero-weight rows are excluded. Stata covariance, means and display-formatting options are not implemented. Use pwcorr() for separate pairwise samples, or pwcorr(.listwise = TRUE) for a common sample with p-values.

levelsof

Distinct values of a variable

Stata

R base

Differs from Stata Store them for a loop: levels <- sort(unique(data$x)), then for (v in levels) { ... }. sort(unique()) excludes NA by default, but string ordering follows R collation and can differ from Stata sorting.

Stata reference · R reference

list

Print every row and column

Stata 

list

R tidystata 

print_headtail(data, n = Inf, width = Inf)

Prints every row and column without storing print preferences. print_headtail(data) shows up to 10 data rows split between the beginning and end, with a row of dots marking an omitted middle; print_interval(data) shows approximately evenly spaced rows without separator rows. Both return the complete input invisibly and keep existing preview preferences. To retain a compact display for later operations, use preview(), preview_headtail() or preview_interval(); unpreview() restores ordinary printing. These helpers keep all data; n controls displayed data rows, not omission markers.

Stata

R stats 

summary(aov(y ~ factor(group), data = data))

Differs from Stata bartlett.test(y ~ group, data = data) gives the equal-variance test that oneway reports. aov() gives the ANOVA table but does not include the Bartlett equal-variance test printed by oneway; request bartlett.test() separately.

pca

Principal components

Stata 

pca x1 x2 x3

R stats 

prcomp(na.omit(select(data, x1, x2, x3)), scale. = TRUE)

Differs from Stata Stata analyses the correlation matrix, so scale. = TRUE matches it. scale. = TRUE matches correlation PCA; signs of eigenvectors are arbitrary and the stored rotations and printed loadings have different normalization conventions.

proportion

Proportion in each category

Stata 

proportion x

R base 

prop.table(table(data$x))

Differs from Stata tab(data, x) shows the same percentages; prop.test() adds a confidence interval for one proportion. The R snippet returns point summaries only (plus SE for mean); Stata also reports confidence intervals and estimation results.

Stata reference · R reference

prtest

Test of a proportion

Stata 

prtest x == 0.5

R stats 

prop.test(sum(data$x == 1, na.rm = TRUE), sum(!is.na(data$x)), p = 0.5, correct = FALSE)

Differs from Stata correct = FALSE gives Stata's normal-approximation test without continuity correction. The uncorrected test statistic matches the normal approximation, but prop.test() confidence intervals use score inversion rather than the prtest Wald interval.

Stata reference · R reference

pwcorr

Pairwise correlations

Stata 

pwcorr x1 x2 x3

R tidystata 

pwcorr(data, x1, x2, x3)

Differs from Stata By default, each pair uses its own complete sample and returns Pearson r, n and p; .wide = TRUE gives a lower-triangular table without n or p. Stata prints a matrix by default and needs sig obs to show p-values and counts. .listwise = TRUE (also Stata casewise) uses one common sample and keeps p-values; corr() uses that sample but omits p. .adjust = "bonferroni" or "sidak" adjusts across all distinct variable pairs separately within each group, including pairs with undefined p-values; adjustment is unavailable with .wide = TRUE. .method = "spearman" gives unweighted pairwise rank correlations; spearman() uses Stata's casewise default. Pearson weights use summed frequency weights or analytic row counts for n; complete zero-weight rows count for analytic n only in pairwise mode. Fractional frequency weights extend Stata's integer convention.

Wilcoxon rank-sum (Mann-Whitney) test

Stata 

ranksum x, by(group)

R stats 

wilcox.test(x ~ group, data = data)

Differs from Stata R can choose exact inference in small samples and applies continuity correction in its normal approximation; Stata defaults differ. Set exact and correct deliberately.

Wilcoxon signed-rank test

Stata

R stats 

wilcox.test(data$x, data$y, paired = TRUE)

Differs from Stata R can choose exact inference in small samples and applies continuity correction in its normal approximation; Stata defaults differ. Set exact and correct deliberately.

sktest

Skewness and kurtosis

Stata 

sktest x

R tidystata 

summ(data, x, .stat = c("skew", "kurtosis"))

For a formal normality test use shapiro.test(data$x).

Stata reference · R reference

spearman

Spearman rank correlation

Stata 

spearman x y

R tidystata 

spearman(data, x, y)

Differs from Stata Uses one common complete-case sample by default, like Stata spearman; .pairwise = TRUE matches spearman, pw. Returns an ungrouped table with var1, var2, r (rho), n and p, plus any grouping keys. P-values follow Stata 18+'s four-moment beta approximation, with a normal fallback for n < 4 or an invalid beta fit; p is NA for n < 3. Ties receive average ranks within each sample. Constant variables give NA, where Stata reports rho = 1. Weights are unsupported. .adjust = "bonferroni" or "sidak" adjusts within each group across all distinct pairs, including undefined p-values; it cannot be combined with .wide = TRUE. Base R cor.test(..., method = "spearman") uses different p-value approximations.

Summary statistics for all variables

Stata reference · R reference

Summary statistics by group

Stata 

bysort group: summarize x

R tidystata 

summ(data, x, .by = group)

Differs from Stata group_by(data, group) |> summ(x) gives the same result. summ() also reports missing counts and has its own default statistic layout; select .stat explicitly when matching Stata output.

Stata reference · R reference

Weighted summary statistics

Stata 

summarize x [aweight = w]

R tidystata 

summ(data, x, .wt = w, .wt_type = "analytic")

Differs from Stata Frequency weights are the default: summ(data, x, .wt = w). summ() also reports missing counts and has its own default statistic layout; select .stat explicitly when matching Stata output.

Stata reference · R reference

Detailed statistics, including percentiles

Stata

R tidystata 

summ(data, x, .detail = TRUE)

Differs from Stata Pick single statistics with .stat, as in summ(data, x, .stat = "p25"). summ() also reports missing counts and has its own default statistic layout; select .stat explicitly when matching Stata output.

tab1

One frequency table per variable

Stata 

tab1 x1 x2 x3

R tidystata 

tab1(data, x1, x2, x3)

Differs from Stata tidystata retains missing categories by default; Stata tabulate excludes them unless missing is specified. Use .missing = FALSE to match Stata. fre1() adds totals and value labels to each one-way table.

Stata reference · R reference

tab2

Cross-tabulation of two variables

Stata 

tab2 x1 x2

R tidystata 

tab2(data, x1, x2)

Differs from Stata With three or more variables, tab2(data, x1, x2, x3) returns every pairwise table, as Stata does. tidystata retains missing categories by default; Stata tabulate excludes them unless missing is specified. Use .missing = FALSE to match Stata. tab2() and fre2() need explicit .by for grouped tables; inherited grouping columns otherwise remain ordinary variables. fre2() displays row value labels, while column headers retain category codes.

Chi-square test of independence
